Definition: a gown (as if hammered out wide)
BiblicalUsage: Pattish is a gown, a garment hammered out wide. It appears once, in Daniel 3:21, among the clothes of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego when they are bound and cast into the burning fiery furnace, in their coats, their hosen, and their hats.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the furnace clothes are named because the men went in dressed as they were, and came out with not a hair singed and their coats unchanged.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace
